16. The paddlewheel was "free-wheeling" and was turning slowly in the current in a counter-
clockwise fashion when observed from the port side of the vessel. The paddlewheel has the
ability to turn on its own when the vessel is moored in an area of strong current.
17. Mr. Staples was unable to steady himself because the paddlewheel was "free-wheeling", and he
fell into the water. He passed under or near the paddlewheel as the current carried him aft. He
was wearing a tan jacket, white Adidas shoes, dark jeans, and a dark undershirt when he fell in.
He was not wearing a lifejacket.
18. Witnesses stated that Mr. Staples was conscious when he emerged on the surface of the water
around ten seconds later. He was moving his arms slowly in the water back and forth. His eyes
were open and he had a surprised expression. He was facing the vessel and did not shout for help.

The vessel's Certificate of Inspection (COI) required three life rings. The vessel had four life

24. The vessel's Station Bill did not indicate that a life ring with a light should be thrown in the water
to mark the position of the man overboard and/or provide the victim with a flotation device.
